title: VERIFY cluster 2 (full adversarial replay): conflicts pass plus seed migration - does it catch the gap it exists for
description: Control-plane full adversarial replay of the conflict-detection pass (T-342) and the four seed precedents (T-343). The decisive question: does the pass detect the harness's own live integrity gap - P-023 applied in code and prose but absent from state.json evolution.accepted_mutations - or does it only pass the fixtures its own author wrote? Build your OWN adversarial registry; reusing the producer's fixtures is self-graded homework. Rotation slot 2 - reviewer identity must differ from T-346's reviewer and from the epic join's (F6), and a different-engine lens is preferred (ORCHESTRATION.md:119-126).
acceptance_criteria: REPLAY: python3 -m unittest discover -s .harness/tests -p "test_precedent*.py" -v - assert a NONZERO executed-test count, QUOTE the 'Ran N tests' line, and confirm the count went UP relative to T-346's run (both new test files must be discovered by this glob); then python3 -m py_compile .harness/bin/precedent.py.

BUILD YOUR OWN ADVERSARIAL REGISTRY in a temporary root - do not reuse the producer's fixtures - containing at minimum: a genuine contradiction pair, an illegitimate lower-tier overruling, a dangling citation, a scope-overlap pair, and a CLEAN control set. Assert ZERO findings on the control (no false positives) and ALL planted conflicts found (no false negatives). Record precision and recall as COUNTS, not adjectives.

CONFIRM THE EXIT-CODE CONTRACT by running the pass in all three states (no conflicts, conflicts found, usage error) and quoting the observed codes; confirm the pass installs no hook and blocks no other CLI (D6: pass, not gate).
RUN the pass against the LIVE seeded registry and record the result. If it reports conflicts among the four seeds, they must be explained rather than suppressed.

AUDIT THE FOUR SEED RECORDS AGAINST THEIR SOURCES: open ORCHESTRATION.md and compare each quoted ratio to the source text (P-023 at :58-67, P-025 at :82-90, P-026 at :211-218, F6 at :119-126) - a paraphrase presented as a quotation is a REJECT; each authority-tier claim must be traceable to the cited file:line; every citation must resolve; scope conditions must be in the UNCONFIRMED state.

CONFIRM THE P-023 RECORD states the integrity gap (applied at .harness/bin/blackboard.py:470 and ORCHESTRATION.md:58, absent from state.json evolution.accepted_mutations, flagged at state.json:791) AND that the task did NOT write state.json - verify with git diff that state.json is untouched apart from blackboard-driven reputation counters. A worker backfilling the P-number ledger unilaterally would be forging a tier-2 constitutional record; if it happened, REJECT and say so.
CONFIRM the seed test reads the live registry without mutating it (git status must show no unexpected registry churn after the test run).
VERDICT T-342 and T-343 with the commands, the counts, and the precision/recall numbers. Reviewer tier: sonnet (P-030). Record the reviewer identity for the F6 rotation audit.

GENUINE GAPS FOUND (beyond AC-2's minimum list; real, via the REAL untampered CLI
where noted, not simulated corruption):
  Case C -- supersedes tier-inversion needs NO tampering at all: a tier-4 record
    supersedes a tier-1 record through the live publish CLI, exit 0, "published
    PR-002", target flips to status=superseded/superseded_by=PR-002. SDR-17.8's
    tier-symmetry refusal (publish items 8-9) and detector 3 both explicitly scope
    themselves to overrules/voids only ("supersedes is deliberately excluded" --
    module docstring). conflicts stays at rc=0, 0 findings. This is a strictly
    stronger finding than det3's own documented tampering-only limitation, because
    it requires zero hand-editing.
  Case D -- detector 2 blind spot on `superseded` (only checks status=='overruled'):
    an ACTIVE record `follows` a target later flipped to status=superseded (via a
    legitimate same-tier supersedes) -> conflicts rc=0, 0 findings, while the active
    record is still citing now-dead law as binding support.
  Case E -- detector 4's scope match is case-sensitive exact-set intersection:
    'role:worker' vs 'Role:Worker', same tier, contradictory ratio, unlinked -> 0
    findings, even though a human reads these as the same scope.
  Case G -- a dangling PR-999/T-999999 reference written ONLY inside free-text
    `dicta` is invisible to both `conflicts` and `cite --record PR-001` (which prints
    only the structured T-330 citation as OK, nothing about the two prose-only
    references) -- `_record_citation_tokens` never reads ratio/dicta/title text.
  Case L (deliberate follow-up on an artifact of my own Case K draft) -- detector 4
    is SUBJECT-AGNOSTIC, unlike detector 1: two same-tier ACTIVE records on
    completely unrelated subjects ('totally-unrelated-topic-alpha' vs '-beta') still
    get flagged purely for sharing the common scope literal 'role:worker' with
    different ratio text. This is a real precision risk at registry scale: scope
    conditions are free-text tags, not a controlled vocabulary, so any two same-tier
    records that happen to share a generic tag like 'role:worker' will collide
    regardless of topical relevance -- unlike detector 1, which is gated on an exact
    `subject` match before it ever compares ratios.
